newsitem.title: FRANCE: Esso France to cut jobs, unions threaten action.
newsitem.headline: Esso France to cut jobs, unions threaten action.

text.p: Esso France, a unit of Exxon Corp, plans to cut about a tenth of its French workforce in a plan to streamline its refining and distribution operations in the face of fierce competition, a spokesman said on Friday.
The plan to shed 217 jobs by the end of 1998, unveiled to workers on Thursday evening, drew immediate union threats of disruption at Esso's two major French oil plants from next week.
The company spokesman said he knew of no threatened action and refineries were running as normal for the time being.
"There will be general assemblies on Monday and the idea is to start a strike movement in the refineries," said a spokesman for the chemicals branch of France's largest union, the CFDT.
Esso France operates a refinery at Fos, near Marseille, with an annual capacity of 5.5 million tonnes, and a 7.5-million-tonne plant near Le Havre in northern France.
It also runs a nationwide network of 1,150 petrol stations.
The CFDT official said unions would fight the Esso France cuts inside its refineries but may also seek support for wider protests against general belt-tightening in the oil industry.
Elf Aquitaine workers have already carried out 24-hour strikes at three refineries in a similar jobs protest and extended their action by another 24 hours on Friday.
The union official said Mobil workers had also worked at minimum safety levels for two hours at a lubricants refinery next to the Esso Le Havre plant on Friday.
A Mobil spokeswoman could not confirm the disruption.
The Esso spokesman said the company's plans to cut staff were needed to cope with refining overcapacity in Europe and what he called "unfair competition" from supermarkets.
European refining profits are at all-time lows.
